title: Experiment Handoff and Responsibility Canvas
content:
Purpose:
This is a working canvas to make cross-functional experiment handoffs explicit for canaries and A/Bs that touch the Console, Serving Runtime, and Routing layers. Primary outcomes: clear owners per phase, what to observe, how to revert, and the short checklist teams can copy into ticket templates.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Owner model: experiment has a single Experiment Lead (product) + Technical Steward (eng) + Ops Steward (SRE/Console).
- Handoff moments: 1) Design -> Infrastructure readiness, 2) Infra ready -> Canary activation, 3) Canary -> Ramp/A/B, 4) Ramp -> Close/rollback.
- Minimum obs: infra health, latency P50/P95, error rate by route, model perf delta vs baseline, cost delta (tokens / GPU-hours), safety signals.

When to use this canvas:
- Multi-team experiments that change routing, model variant, or cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Rollouts where fallback logic or automatic revert is enabled.
- Any A/B with >1% global traffic or that affects billing materially.

Experiment roles (recommended):
- Experiment Lead (product): owns hypothesis, success metrics, stakeholder comms.
- Technical Steward (eng-serving-runtime): implements routing, model pins, rollout config, metrics hooks.
- Ops Steward (eng-sre/console): configures canary slices, synthetic traffic, thresholds and automated revert.
- Data/ML Analyst: creates evaluation slices, post-run analysis, and sampling plan.
- Customer Success / Legal (if impacted): sign off for privacy, contracts, or high-risk customers.

Handoff checkpoints (copy into ticket checklist):
1) Design -> Infra readiness (pre-implementation)
   - Owner: Experiment Lead -> Technical Steward
   - Deliverables: experiment brief (hypothesis, metrics, slice defs), target traffic proportions, estimated cost impact, compliance considerations, list of routes/users excluded.
   - Infra checks: necessary model variants available; quantization/stateful cache flags set; config for fallbacks exists.
   - Jira links: include RDW ticket (e.g., JIRA-RDW-2371)

2) Infra ready -> Canary activation (pre-exposure)
   - Owner: Technical Steward -> Ops Steward
   - Deliverables: rollout config (canary slice ids), synthetic traffic plan, monitoring dashboard link, automation playbook for revert.
   - Ops checklist: confirm canary throttles, circuit breaker thresholds, alert receivers, runbook on-call rotation, and synthetic job scheduled.
   - Confident? If any infra test fails, mark status "blocked" and do not proceed.

3) Canary -> Ramp/A-B (during exposure)
   - Owner: Ops Steward -> Experiment Lead (shared)
   - Deliverables: daily pulse notes, telemetric snapshot (first 4 hours), decision log for ramp increments.
   - Observation windows: 15m (fast health), 1h (quality signals), 24h (cost/usage & user feedback).
   - Gate rules (example):
     - No step-up unless P95 latency delta < 10% and error rate delta < 0.2% for last 60m.
     - If model perf (key metric) drops >2% on primary slice, revert immediately and notify stakeholders.

4) Ramp -> Close or Rollback (post-exposure)
   - Owner: Experiment Lead
   - Deliverables: final analysis, recommendation (ship, iterate, rollback). Create follow-up tickets for remediation.
   - Archive: capture experiment config, seed prompts, key charts, and rollback trigger artifacts to Confluence.

Decision matrix (quick):
- Safety-critical regression (safety / hallucination): immediate rollback + incident.
- Latency / cost increases without quality wins: pause + optimize routing or quantization settings.
- Small quality improvements with cost increases: escalate to product for ROI decision.

Minimal telemetry list (must publish to dashboards before activation):
- infra.node.cpu/gpu_utilization (per cluster)
- request.latency.{p50,p95,p99} by route and model variant
- request.error_rate (4xx/5xx) by route
- model.delta_metric (experiment - baseline) by slice (e.g., rerank NDCG, accuracy)
- token_consumption.rate and estimated GPU-hours per 1k requests
- user_feedback.rate (opt-in flag sampling)

Template: quick runbook excerpt to paste in ticket body:
---
Experiment: <short name>
Experiment Lead: <name>
Technical Steward: <name>
Ops Steward: <name>
Slices: <json list of slice ids or brief defs>
Canary window: <duration>
Success criteria: <primary metric + delta + confidence window>
Rollback criteria: <list of thresholds>
Dashboards: <link>
Synthetic jobs: <link>
Automation: <link to revert playbook or webhook>
---

Communication plan (practical templates):
- Slack: #rollouts - post at activation, summary every 2h during first day, and final status. Use emoji flags: :green_heart: for OK, :warning: for watch, :rotating_light: for rollback.
- Email to stakeholders: one-pager after 24h with signals and recommendation.
- On-call: Ops Steward to own immediate revert; Experiment Lead to coordinate stakeholder comms.

Friction & open decisions (notes):
- Who will own cost anomalies if an experiment is run by a product buddy but causes spike? Proposal: billing ops tags charge-back to the owning product team for first 3 months of rollout.
- Confidence windows: For long-tailed user slices (enterprise customers), 24h may not be enough. Consider extended observation windows per slice.
- Synthetic traffic coverage: how to simulate rare behavior (edge prompts)? Need repo of seed prompts maintained by ML Analysts.

Post-mortem checklist (if rollback or incident):
- Capture timeline (activation, alerts, decision to revert)
- Attach sampling of problem requests and model outputs
- Root cause hypothesis (infra/config/model)
- Action items: ownership + deadline + follow-up ticket IDs
- Communication: who notified which customers and legal sign-off if required

Quick examples (embedding into real flow):
- Example A: new quantized model reduces cost by 35% but increases P95 by 12% on short-context routes. Decision: pause ramp, enable prefix-KV caching for those routes, re-evaluate.
- Example B: reranker variant improves NDCG by 3% on search slice but increases token use by 8%. Decision: product to run ROI calc; if positive, move to dedicated capacity to stabilize latency.

Action items (right now):
- [ ] Add this canvas to experiment ticket template (Jin)
- [ ] Create a dashboard template with minimal telemetry (Samir)
- [ ] Populate seed prompt repo with 30 examples for edge slices (Data team)
- [ ] Finalize charge-back proposal for cost anomalies (Finance + Product)

Notes to self / working thoughts:
- Keep this lean — teams want a checklist they can copy/paste. Avoid over-prescription for small rapid experiments.
- Consider a "fast-mode" variant of this canvas for sub-1% traffic experiments (reduced telemetry + 4h observation).
- Should we bake automatic gating into the Console as a default experiment policy? Idea: a toggle that enforces gate rules and automates reverts if triggered. Needs product + legal review.

Scratch: Slack shortcuts to ping on revert - @ops-lead, @experiment-lead, #rollouts

References and useful links:
- Experiment framework confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EX/experiment-framework
- RDW-2371 (routing rollout for reranker)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/482 (sample rollout templates)

End of canvas. Paste this into experimental tickets and iterate.
